title: Publication Profile
description:
Validates files in core/reference/publication/. How a release reaches one portal: the submission method the portal supports, the console a deterministic browser run drives when it supports no API, what only a person can do there, and whether automated use of the console is permitted by the portal's terms.

DATA, not integration code: the publish step's adapters read it, and the pipeline never names a portal. Kept apart from core/reference/platforms/<id>.yaml on purpose - a platform profile is pinned by content hash by every game built against it and changes only with the portal's compliance rules; this changes with the portal's console and is pinned by a publication record, never by a game.

Nothing here is a credential. Credentials are named (an environment variable the installation sets) and never written.

id.description: The platform id: core/reference/platforms/<id>.yaml must exist.

status.description: unverified: the console flow below has not been exercised against the live portal by a person; the publish step then stops HUMAN_REQUIRED before contacting it.

method.description: The portal's supported way in, preferred in this order: an official API or CLI when the portal publishes one; the developer console by a deterministic browser run when it does not; email or manual when neither exists. Never an undocumented API.

api.description: method api/cli only: the documented endpoint or tool, by name.

console.description: method console only: the console a browser run drives. Origins are the only ones the browser may reach; everything else is refused at the browser.

automation_terms.description: Whether the portal's terms allow automated use of its developer console, as a person established from the portal's own documents. unverified or prohibited: the publish step never drives the console and stops HUMAN_REQUIRED (reason terms-unconfirmed); an installation records a person's finding in factory.publish.platforms.<id>.terms_confirmed.

terms_checked.description: Who established automation_terms, when, from which document.

credential.description: The credential the adapter needs and where the installation keeps it - by variable NAME only. A storage state is a Playwright storageState JSON a person captured by logging in once; the step never types a password.

capture.description: How a person captures or rotates it.

human_required.description: What this portal makes a person do, whatever the method: login and its challenges, accepting terms, payout setup, a console switch the automation does not touch.

constraints.description: Portal rules an adapter checks before acting.

postpone_publication.description: The portal can hold a verified draft unpublished; the adapter sets it so publication timing stays a person's.

verification.description: How the portal's own state is read back after acting: the states its console shows, and which of them mean what.
